title: Impact of Unexpected CEO Departures on Stock Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Method: Event Study.  
Why: The treatment (unexpected CEO departure) is a sharply dated, idiosyncratic event for each firm. We want to measure abnormal stock‐price reactions in a narrow window around day 0. Event studies isolate the causal effect as long as markets are efficient and no other firm–specific news contaminates the window.

Key assumptions  
1. Unanticipated event: investors did not foresee the CEO exit, so no pre‐trending abnormal returns should appear.  
2. Market efficiency (semi-strong form): prices instantly incorporate all public information, so any abnormal return in the event window is attributable to the departure.  
3. No confounding events for the same firm inside the chosen window.  
4. The market model estimated in a clean pre-event window (-10 to -3 here) captures expected returns correctly.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Required packages
library(dplyr)
library(broom)

# --- 1. Load data -------------------------------------------------------------
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s54_data.csv")

# --- 2. Define windows --------------------------------------------------------
est_win  <- -10:-3   # estimation window to get alpha & beta
evt_win1 <- -1:1     # main event window ([-1,+1])
evt_win2 <- -3:3     # robustness window ([-3,+3])

# --- 3. Estimate market model and compute abnormal returns -------------------
# Helper that returns a tibble with abnormal returns
get_abnormal <- function(data){
  # 3a. Estimate alpha & beta in estimation window
  est_data <- filter(data, event_day %in% est_win)
  mod <- lm(ret ~ mkt_ret, data = est_data)
  coefs <- tidy(mod)
  alpha <- coefs$estimate[coefs$term=="(Intercept)"]
  beta  <- coefs$estimate[coefs$term=="mkt_ret"]
  
  # 3b. Abnormal returns in all days available
  data %>%
    mutate(alpha = alpha,
           beta_fitted = beta,
           ar = ret - (alpha + beta * mkt_ret))
}

df_ar <- df %>% group_by(stock_id) %>% group_modify(~get_abnormal(.x))

# --- 4. Cumulative Abnormal Returns ------------------------------------------
car_fun <- function(win){
  df_ar %>% 
    filter(event_day %in% win) %>% 
    group_by(stock_id) %>% 
    summarise(CAR = sum(ar)) %>% 
    ungroup()
}

car_1 <- car_fun(evt_win1)
car_2 <- car_fun(evt_win2)

# --- 5. Statistical inference -------------------------------------------------
t_test_1 <- t.test(car_1$CAR)
t_test_2 <- t.test(car_2$CAR)

# --- 6. Alternate abnormal return metric: market-adjusted ---------------------
df_adj <- df %>%
  mutate(ar_ma = ret - mkt_ret)

car_ma1 <- df_adj %>% filter(event_day %in% evt_win1) %>% 
  group_by(stock_id) %>% summarise(CAR = sum(ar_ma)) %>% ungroup()

t_test_ma1 <- t.test(car_ma1$CAR)

# --- 7. Print concise results -------------------------------------------------
cat("Main window ([-1,+1]) – Market model\n")
cat("Mean CAR:", round(mean(car_1$CAR)*100,3), "%\n")
cat("t-statistic:", round(t_test_1$statistic,3),
    "  p-value:", round(t_test_1$p.value,4), "\n\n")

cat("Robustness window ([-3,+3]) – Market model\n")
cat("Mean CAR:", round(mean(car_2$CAR)*100,3), "%\n")
cat("t-statistic:", round(t_test_2$statistic,3),
    "  p-value:", round(t_test_2$p.value,4), "\n\n")

cat("Alternate abnormal returns (market-adjusted)  –  window [-1,+1]\n")
cat("Mean CAR:", round(mean(car_ma1$CAR)*100,3), "%\n")
cat("t-statistic:", round(t_test_ma1$statistic,3),
    "  p-value:", round(t_test_ma1$p.value,4), "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Sign: Negative. An unexpected CEO exit typically raises uncertainty about leadership and strategy, so investors mark down firm value.  
Magnitude: Around −1 % to −2 % cumulative abnormal return over the 3-day window (≈ −0.5 % per day), implying a statistically significant t-statistic in the range of −2 to −3.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare stock returns before and after the CEO departure event.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The unexpected CEO departure is associated with a positive cumulative abnormal return.
